summary: The run is valid. All nine acceptance checks passed against the actual simulated values. At the end of the 1 s run the model reports mmf_At=1000 A-turn, Phi_core_Wb=0.000228479 Wb, B_core_T=B_gap_T=0.571199 T, Vm_core_At=90.9091 A-turn, and Vm_gap_At=909.091 A-turn, all within the stated tolerances. The mmf also starts at zero and reaches the required full-current level during the run. The final magnetic potential balance check passes with a relative residual of about 1.0e-7, far inside the 0.005 limit. The reported min/max/final values are consistent with the intended ramp-up from 0 to 0.1 s and steady hold afterward, although that whole-trajectory shape was not itself defined as a mechanically checkable acceptance criterion beyond the endpoint and attainment checks.
assumptions: The excitation current schedule was imposed as a prescribed input: linear ramp from 0 A at 0 s to 2 A at 0.1 s, then held at 2 A through 1 s.
1000 output intervals were used over the 1 s simulation window.
No additional mechanically evaluable monotonic-rise or hold checks were added beyond the listed acceptance criteria.
The generated model replaced invalid connect() usage on scalar report variable Phi_core_Wb with equation assignments, treating it as an ordinary Real rather than a connector.
Each named physical unit was kept as its own top-level component instance rather than aggregating the plant.
The prescribed excitation current was implemented as a Modelica.Blocks.Sources.Ramp with height=2 A, duration=0.1 s, offset=0 A, startTime=0 s.
Experiment Interval was set to 0.001 s and solver Tolerance to 1e-6; the tolerance value is a modeling assumption because the brief did not specify it.

The brief did not provide a magnetic connector topology or a FluxTubes mapping for the custom magnetic reference entities, so these were preserved as separately inspectable signal-level components rather than mapped to an unstated connector network.

Derived from the final values, the model behavior is consistent with a linear magnetic-circuit calculation using fixed reluctances for the iron core and air gap; no nonlinear B-H behavior, saturation, hysteresis, leakage flux, fringing, or dynamic inductive effects appear in the reported results.
